body: Réunion is an overseas department of France, located in the Indian Ocean east of Madagascar. For country streak purposes, it is counted as France.
The Réunion Street View car has a visible roof rack and black tape at the end of the rear right bar. Do not confuse this with the Ghana car, which has tape on the front right bar.
As a French Department, Réunion features French infrastructure, including signs, bollards, and poles.
Réunion is a mountainous, volcanic island with lush green mountains. Vegetation consists of palms, ferns, and pine trees at higher elevations.
Street View coverage is limited, with only a few roads covered by car. Most of the island is covered by trekker.
Réunion has six distinct bus stop designs: Yellow (most common), L-shaped (white or olive), Pink, Orange, Green, and Red. Their distribution across the island can help with region-guessing.
Sugarcane plantations are found in the northeast and southwest of Réunion. The southwest is generally more populated.
Cilaos is a town located inside a caldera. It is recognizable by the surrounding wall of mountains and generally overcast coverage.
A distinct rectangular blur is visible on the front camera in all coverage north of Saint-Louis.
The northwestern section of the N1 is a divided highway. It features a distinct ridge to the southeast and the ocean to the northwest.
The Route du Volcan is characterized by its Martian landscape, with brown-red soil and sparse vegetation. Look for white stones lining the road.
A specific forest road is a winding dirt track with dense vegetation, including pine and eucalyptus trees. The track is dark with grass growing in the middle.
The eastern N2 passes through the least populated part of the island. It's a single carriageway surrounded by either dense vegetation or a vast, nearly treeless landscape.
The two largest towns can be differentiated by their bollards. Saint Paul uses black bollards, while the capital, Saint Denis, uses green bollards, often with white balls on top.
